Gentlemans, during combat, damage with elements is calculated incorrectly.
I changed the Game_battler item_element_rate so that while the attribute effectiveness coefficient was being calculated, conditions were being added/removed from me.
Ruby:
def item_element_rate(user, item)
    $game_variables[15] = user.features_set(FEATURE_ATK_ELEMENT)
    $game_variables[16] = item.damage.element_id
    $game_variables[17] = element_rate(item.damage.element_id)
    case item.damage.element_id
      when 7 #earth
      result = user.atk_elements.empty? ? 1.0 : elements_max_rate(user.atk_elements)
      if state?(29)
        add_state(33)
        remove_state(29)
      end
      if state?(30)
        add_state(26)
        remove_state(30)
      else
        remove_state(26)
      end
    return result
      when 3 #fire
      result = user.atk_elements.empty? ? 1.0 : elements_max_rate(user.atk_elements)
      if state?(27)
        add_state(31)
        remove_state(27)
      end
      if state?(32)
        add_state(28)
        remove_state(32)
      else
        remove_state(28)
      end
    return result
      when 4 #frost
      result = user.atk_elements.empty? ? 1.0 : elements_max_rate(user.atk_elements)
      if state?(28)
        add_state(32)
        remove_state(28)
        end
      if state?(31)
        add_state(27)
        remove_state(31)
      else
        remove_state(27)
      end
    return result
        when 8 #air
      result = user.atk_elements.empty? ? 1.0 : elements_max_rate(user.atk_elements)
      if state?(26)
        add_state(30)
        remove_state(26)
      end
      if state?(33)
        add_state(29)
        remove_state(33)
      else
        remove_state(29)
      end
    return result
  else element_rate(item.damage.element_id)
  end
  $game_variables[18] = result
  end
But when I entered battle, conditions were being added/removed, but the damage of my attribute-based skills didn't change on targets with attribute effectiveness.
Ruby:
def make_damage_value(user, item)
    value = item.damage.eval(user, self, $game_variables)
    $game_variables[19] = value
    value *= item_element_rate(user, item)
    $game_variables[20] = value
    value *= pdr if item.physical?
    value *= mdr if item.magical?
    value *= rec if item.damage.recover?
    value = apply_critical(value) if @result.critical
    value = apply_variance(value, item.damage.variance)
    value = apply_guard(value)
    $game_variables[21] = value
    @result.make_damage(value.to_i, item)
  end
I added lines so that the values were written to game_variables, but that didn't help me figure out the problem.
Because after looking at the variables, I saw that
variable 17 = 0.0
variable 18 = 0
variable 19 = 800
variable 20 = 800.0
even though variable 20 should be 0 and damage 0 when the expression value *= item_element_rate(user, item) was executed, where item_element_rate(user, item) is 0.
Help me find the error. PLZ
UPD
I noticed that the lines value *= pdr if item.physical? and value *= mdr if item.magical? don't change the value regardless of the value. It's as if the value doesn't change at all and the damage is dealt according to the formula.

posts.author: Timtrack
posts.body:
Hello,
din676 said:
even though variable 20 should be 0 and damage 0 when the expression value *= item_element_rate(user, item) was executed, where item_element_rate(user, item) is 0.
Help me find the error. PLZ
Click to expand...
Can you give more context to the skill/item you used? Like which elements did you use?
Just so you know, variable 18 will almost always be 0 in your code unless your item element is neither 3,4,7 nor 8. The reason why is because no lines will be executed after performing a
return
in a method, so
$game_variables[18] = result
will not be executed, in fact, if it is executed by using another element, then your game is likely to crash because
result
does not exist.
So I suspect you did not have any specific element rate for the target and the result of
item_element_rate
is indeed
1.0
.
din676 said:
I noticed that the lines value *= pdr if item.physical? and value *= mdr if item.magical? don't change the value regardless of the value.
Click to expand...
Unless
pdr
or
mdr
were modified by the target (being general physical resistance or magical resistance), then they won't change the value because they are
1.0
by default, so not a bug.
As a side note, you should probably avoid modifying states when calling
item_element_rate
as it may be used outside of using the item or skill, which could create some weird behaviors.
I suggest you use the state modification before or after the use of your item.
Here is a modified version of your code by me, I removed the variables modifications, synthetized some of your code and moved the states change to a more proper place:
Ruby:
class Game_Battler < Game_BattlerBase
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # new method: convert_state -> turn original state into another if the state
  # is here
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def convert_state(original_state, new_state)
    return unless state?(original_state)
    add_state(new_state)
    remove_state(original_state)
  end
 
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # new method: element4_states
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  def element4_states(element_id)
    case element_id
    when 3 #fire
      convert_state(27, 31)
      convert_state(32, 28)
    when 4 # frost
      convert_state(28, 32)
      convert_state(31, 27)
    when 7 #earth
      convert_state(29, 33)
      convert_state(30, 26)
    when 8 #air
      convert_state(26, 30)
      convert_state(33, 29)
    end
  end
 
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # alias method: item_element_rate -> 4 base elements (3,4,7,8) are handled
  # like attack element (comment: not recommended to use this modified method)
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  alias tim_elem4_item_element_rate item_element_rate
  def item_element_rate(user, item)
    case item.damage.element_id
    when 3,4,7,8 #if element if one of the main 4:
      user.atk_elements.empty? ? 1.0 : elements_max_rate(user.atk_elements)
    else #default behavior if another element is used:
      tim_elem4_item_element_rate(user,item)
    end
  end
 
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # alias method: item_apply -> states are modified if item has hit self
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  alias tim_elem4_item_apply item_apply
  def item_apply(user, item)
    tim_elem4_item_apply(user, item) #call original method
    element4_states(item.damage.element_id) if @result.hit?
  end
end #Game_Battler

What is the hit type of the skill you used?
If it is "certain hit", then pdr and mdr won't apply. You can check the hit type of a skill like this:
(also note that fdr is floor damage rate, which is related to map damage)
Edit: A good way to check if there is a database issue is to test your skill on a project with no script.
You should be able to see if there is an issue. If there is, it is very likely to be a mistake in your parameters.
Then, if it worked, you can test the skill in your project but without your script or mine, if it does not work, then it's probably another script from your project that mess things up.
Finally, if it worked for both cases, then this is indeed an issue with both mine and your code. I really think removing the modifications to
item_element_rate
should do the trick.
